reason: Premises 1 and 2 are directly supported by E1, and premise 3 by E2, but premise 4 (thermal aging to stabilize/enhance both nanotwins and vermicular phases) and premise 5 (simultaneous improvement of all four properties) lack any cited evidence and are speculative extensions beyond the cited works.
premises: Laser surface heat treatment at ~1000 °C and 4 mm/s produces an inverse gradient-grained structure with a partially recrystallized hard core and hierarchical nanotwins in CoCrFeMnNi HEA.
This gradient + nanotwin structure enhances strength–ductility synergy via hetero-deformation-induced strengthening.
A kinked vermicular eutectic microstructure can be formed in an (AlCrFe₂)₆₅Ni₃₅ EMPEA and improves strength–ductility synergy over straight morphologies.
A subsequent thermal aging step can stabilize and enhance hierarchical nanotwins and vermicular eutectic phases in the gradient structure.
Combining these features into one multi-stage process will simultaneously improve yield strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance.
